newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds finish much higher on growth hopes.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds finish much higher on growth hopes.

text.p: Argentine bonds closed much higher Thursday on increasing optimism the economy is rebounding and on stronger U.S. Treasuries.

A trader at a large Argentine bank said "if the economy grows the deficit will narrow," and that may help reduce the supply of bonds. On Wednesday the Economy Ministry announced higher-than-expected growth in the third quarter of 6.6 percent compared with the same period a year earlier.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 5/8 to 84-1/2, while the local dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.80 to 120.60.

But traders voiced surprise at the surge this session, considering the release of Brazilian October trade figures showing a deficit of $1.308 billion. Earlier in the week traders were concerned that such a large figure could upset Latin American markets.
"I don't know why - because the market is that way," commented another trader, in search of an explanation.
If anything, noted the first trader, the fact that Argentine and other Latin American bonds were not upset by the Brazilian trade news showed underlying strength.
Activity picked up during the session, and a turnaround in U.S. Treasuries from early declines supported the rise.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 7.55 percent from 7.45 percent.
